_note: BIOLOGY ONLY. Compiled from general spearfishing-guide sources (not a validated regional survey), for the temperate/subtropical Western Australian reef fauna around Rottnest and Perth. Depth, temperature, substrate and season of presence and how each species responds to water clarity. None of it is law - Western Australia has its own detailed size/bag rules, and Rottnest Island itself is a marine reserve with several no-take sanctuary zones that are not encoded anywhere in this app.

species.note: WA-endemic and the region's headline reef fish - deep, structure-holding, slow-growing and long-lived, which is exactly why it is so vulnerable to overfishing. Occasionally taken shallower but the good ones sit deep.
Long-lived (decades) and wide-ranging over both reef and sand near structure. Cockburn Sound to the south is an important breeding ground, so numbers and size skew seasonally.
WA's amberjack - deep reef structure, a strong, aggressive fighter, occasionally taken from shallower ledges near Rottnest.
WA-endemic wrasse, resident on reef structure, sought after for its eating quality as much as its scarcity.
WA-endemic small grouper, shallower and more approachable than dhufish or samson - a good structure-holding species for the shallower caves and ledges close to Rottnest itself.

_legal_note: Legal rules live in legal/<JURISDICTION>.json and are merged in at run time. No legal pack exists yet for AU-WA, so this app will correctly show 'not researched' rather than any size or season claim - the WA Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) publishes the real rules, and Rottnest Island's own sanctuary zones (e.g. Parker Point, Salmon Bay, Little Salmon Bay) ban all fishing including spearfishing outright, which this app does not currently mask out.
